events.title: Navigate to example.test
events.summary: The application turns a human hostname into a network dependency graph.
events.detail: A URL is intent, not a route. HOPSCOTCH starts at the application layer and moves outward only when the next dependency requires it.

events.title: DNS cache miss
events.summary: No usable cached answer exists for this curated journey.
events.detail: The simulated miss forces the complete recursive resolution path to remain visible.

events.title: Stub asks recursive resolver
events.summary: A recursive A query is issued for example.test.
events.detail: The stub asks one recursive resolver to finish the job. The recursive resolver performs iterative upstream work.

events.title: Root referral received
events.summary: The recursive resolver learns where to continue the namespace walk.
events.detail: A referral narrows the search to the next authority.

events.title: TLD referral received
events.summary: The recursive resolver is directed toward the authoritative zone.
events.detail: The resolver continues iteratively rather than asking the browser to chase each authority.

events.title: example.test → 203.0.113.42
events.summary: The authoritative answer supplies a documentation-only destination address for the deterministic story.
events.detail: 203.0.113.0/24 is documentation space. This journey never implies that example.test is a live public host.

events.title: Answer cached
events.summary: The recursive result becomes reusable until its simulated TTL expires.
events.detail: The cache starts at a deterministic 300-second TTL and ages with Journey time.

events.title: Destination enters the routing table
events.summary: 203.0.113.42 requires a next-hop decision outside the local subnet.
events.detail: The camera moves outward because an IP destination cannot leave the host until a route and next hop exist.

events.title: Default gateway selected
events.summary: The host has a viable local path to the router that can forward toward the Internet.
events.detail: This is a deterministic teaching topology, not a measurement of the viewer’s LAN.

events.title: Interdomain path context appears
events.summary: A simulated valley-free AS path carries the story beyond the local routing domain.
events.detail: The AS path is SIMULATED. Public collector paths, when attached, remain separate evidence and never replace this story path.

events.title: Physical infrastructure comes into view
events.summary: Interconnection facilities give geography to the story without claiming a cable or exact forwarding path.
events.detail: PeeringDB facility points can decorate this moment as PUBLIC DATA. Any connecting great-circle geometry remains INFERRED.

events.title: SYN leaves the client
events.summary: TCP opens a reliable byte stream before TLS begins.
events.detail: This branch uses TCP + TLS 1.3 + HTTP/2.

events.title: SYN-ACK returns
events.summary: The server acknowledges the client sequence space and contributes its own initial sequence number.
events.detail: The handshake establishes shared transport sequence state.

events.title: TCP connection established
events.summary: The third handshake segment makes the bidirectional byte stream usable.
events.detail: Encryption still does not exist yet.

events.title: ClientHello
events.summary: SNI names example.test; ALPN offers h2.
events.detail: TLS records are carried inside the established TCP byte stream.

events.title: ServerHello
events.summary: The server selects compatible cryptographic parameters and contributes its key share.
events.detail: The transcript now contains both hellos.

events.title: Handshake traffic becomes encrypted
events.summary: EncryptedExtensions and later server handshake messages are protected with handshake keys.
events.detail: HOPSCOTCH shows named key-schedule stages, not invented secret bytes.

events.title: Certificate identity validated
events.summary: The presented identity is checked against example.test.
events.detail: Certificate validation authenticates the server identity independently from routing.

events.title: Application traffic keys ready
events.summary: Both sides can now protect application data with TLS 1.3 application traffic secrets.
events.detail: The encryption boundary changes before HTTP/2 request data is sent.

events.title: HTTP/2 control state exchanged
events.summary: SETTINGS establishes connection-level HTTP/2 parameters over the encrypted stream.
events.detail: HTTP/2 multiplexing lives above TCP.

events.title: GET / on example.test
events.summary: Request headers become an encrypted HTTP/2 HEADERS frame carried by TLS over TCP.
events.detail: Each representation is a different abstraction of the same bytes.

events.title: Application data isolated
events.summary: HTTP/2 request headers for GET / on example.test becomes the logical payload.
events.detail: This is the clear application meaning at the browser boundary; it is not yet a wire-visible packet.

events.title: TLS 1.3 application data closes
events.summary: HTTP/2 request bytes become opaque TLS application data.
events.detail: The HTTP meaning remains available above TLS; packet observers without keys see an opaque TLS record payload.

events.title: TCP segment assembles
events.summary: TCP ports, sequence space, flags, window, and checksum surround the protected bytes.
events.detail: TLS-protected bytes become TCP payload. Sequence, acknowledgment, flags, window, and checksum belong to the TCP header.

events.title: IPv4 envelope assembles
events.summary: Source, destination, TTL, protocol, length, and checksum establish the routed packet.
events.detail: The IP packet is the continuity object across routed hops. Its Ethernet envelope may change at every hop.

events.title: Hop-local Ethernet envelope closes
events.summary: Source and next-hop destination MAC addresses frame the same IPv4 packet for this local link.
events.detail: The Ethernet header is hop-local. The NIC generates the FCS during transmission; the simulated inspection snapshot does not pretend the trailer was captured.

events.title: Structured frame ready at the NIC
events.summary: Five semantic representations collapse into one deterministic outbound data unit.
events.detail: No animation callback created this frame. Scrubbing to this timestamp reconstructs the same semantic assembly from the canonical event log.

events.title: NIC serializes the structured frame
events.summary: The frame becomes an ordered link transmission without changing its packet semantics.
events.detail: The renderer exposes bytes, bits, and link activity as representations of one deterministic frame. The NIC generates a per-transmission FCS; it is not fabricated as captured packet data.

events.title: Symbols cross the access link
events.summary: Structured bytes become physical link activity moving toward the switch.
events.detail: Serialization is a rendering of the already-built frame. Browser scheduling cannot create, drop, or reorder semantic network state.

events.title: Switch isolates destination MAC
events.summary: Only the destination MAC is projected for the forwarding decision; unrelated packet fields recede.
events.detail: The switch may learn the source MAC on ingress, but this forwarding decision compares destination MAC 02:48:4F:50:00:02 with its MAC table.

events.title: MAC table selects Gi0/24
events.summary: The same Ethernet header and IPv4 payload leave the selected switch port.
events.detail: A normal Layer 2 forward does not rewrite source or destination MAC. The egress transmitter generates link-local physical overhead such as a new FCS.

events.title: Router terminates the incoming Ethernet envelope
events.summary: The hop-local Layer 2 shell opens and ends; the routed IPv4 packet remains.
events.detail: The router validates the incoming frame, removes the Ethernet header/trailer context, and makes an IP forwarding decision. Ethernet does not continue through the router.

events.title: TTL decrements: 64 → 63
events.summary: The router mutates the IPv4 TTL and updates the IPv4 header checksum.
events.detail: Destination IP and transport payload remain logically continuous. TTL and its dependent header checksum are the exact routed-hop mutations shown here.

events.title: Destination IP selects the next hop
events.detail: The destination IP—not either hop-local MAC address—selects the route. The chosen next hop will supply the next Ethernet destination.

events.title: A new Ethernet envelope assembles
events.summary: Router wan0 constructs new source and next-hop destination MAC fields around the forwarded IPv4 packet.
events.detail: The outgoing frame is a new hop-local object. The IPv4 continuity identity survives with TTL 63 and an updated header checksum.

events.title: The re-encapsulated packet continues
events.summary: A second link transmission carries the new Ethernet frame toward 198.51.100.2.
events.detail: The visual grammar repeats—frame, serialization, link—but the Layer 2 addresses now belong to the next hop while the IP destination remains 203.0.113.42.

events.title: Response headers arrive
events.summary: The origin begins the response with status and metadata before the body streams.
events.detail: The first response bytes do not mean transfer is complete.

events.title: Response DATA streams
events.summary: Encrypted application data crosses the established TCP stream.
events.detail: HOPSCOTCH can now zoom into one representative frame.

events.title: Freeze one TCP frame
events.summary: One delivery unit becomes the entire world: link, network, transport, and encrypted TLS payload bytes.
events.detail: The packet microscope is a projection of the same Journey moment.

events.title: Explode TCP/IP headers
events.summary: The same frame opens into persistent link, network, transport, security, and application objects.
events.detail: TLS-protected application bytes remain opaque at this packet-observation boundary.

events.title: Transfer acknowledged
events.summary: The representative response flight is cumulatively acknowledged and TCP delivery is complete.
events.detail: The camera pulls back because byte delivery has finished.

events.title: Response available to the application
events.summary: Decrypted response bytes are delivered upward to the browser.
events.detail: Network delivery ends by satisfying the application intent that began the story.

events.title: Pull back through the route
events.summary: The journey recedes from application state to the forwarding structures that carried it.
events.detail: Nothing new is transmitted here. This is an explanatory camera move through already completed causal state.

events.title: Return to Internet scale
events.summary: Local routes, AS policy, and physical infrastructure collapse back into one global context.
events.detail: Observed/public context can decorate this endpoint view without rewriting the simulated journey that just completed.

events.title: example.test journey complete
events.summary: A human hostname became DNS state, routing state, transport state, protected application traffic, packets, and finally a response.
events.detail: The same global time machine can now be rewound to any causal boundary without changing the event log.
